rotations.summary: Conservative: Grass cover crop – Corn – Wheat – Soybean: rank 1 of 7, 81 points (range 71–93).
rotations.why: This rotation is recommended because it adds plant cover in winter, diversifies the system (4 distinct crops vs. 3) and cuts months of bare soil (from 3.5 to 1.5 per year). It has the highest score with balanced priorities. However, it increases estimated water demand (10 % more than the current one) and requires terminate the cover crop in August so it does not use the fallow's water.
risks: Water-deficit risk: rain and stored water cover only 47 % of demand.
The weather used is a SIMULATED sample: scores are illustrative until NASA POWER is queried.

rotations.summary: Recommended mix: Wheat/second-crop soybean – vetch – corn: rank 2 of 7, 80 points (range 70–92).
rotations.why: Compared with the current rotation, this alternative adds plant cover in winter, diversifies the system (4 distinct crops vs. 3), adds legumes that supply nitrogen, cuts months of bare soil (from 3.5 to 1.0 per year) and lowers the crops' exposure to drought, heat and pest or disease problems. It ranks 2 of 7: compared with the first, it loses mostly on water resilience (46 vs. 51). However, it increases estimated water demand (15 % more than the current one), requires terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop and requires check soil-profile water at wheat planting: the double crop only pays off if water is stored.
risks: Water-deficit risk: rain and stored water cover only 46 % of demand.
The weather used is a SIMULATED sample: scores are illustrative until NASA POWER is queried.

rotations.why: Compared with the current rotation, this alternative adds plant cover in winter, diversifies the system (4 distinct crops vs. 3), adds legumes that supply nitrogen, cuts months of bare soil (from 3.5 to 1.0 per year) and lowers the crops' exposure to drought, heat and pest or disease problems. rotations.summary: Corn – peanut – wheat/second-crop soybean: rank 4 of 7, 74 points (range 63–85).
rotations.why: Compared with the current rotation, this alternative diversifies the system (4 distinct crops vs. 3) and cuts months of bare soil (from 3.5 to 4.0 per year). It ranks 4 of 7: compared with the first, it loses mostly on soil health (53 vs. 84). However, it lowers estimated relative income, requires secure a sales contract for the peanut and requires plant the second-crop soybean as soon as the wheat is harvested.

However, it lowers estimated relative income, requires plan a four-year sequence and requires terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop.
